questions.questionText: Which statement about the factors of production is correct?

options.text: A river from which a company draws water is called land.
Raising finance for a company is called capital.
Supervisors employed in a company are called enterprise.
The owner of a company is called labour.

questions.questionText: Which terms summarise the nature of the economic problem?

options.text: finite resources and limited wants
finite resources and unlimited wants
infinite resources and limited wants
infinite resources and unlimited wants

questions.questionText:
The government of a country with a rapidly increasing population decides to switch resources
from investment to increased subsidies to farmers.
What is the opportunity cost of this decision?

options.text: the profit earned by farmers
the rent of the land on which food is grown
the reduction in investment
the wages of the farm workers

questions.questionText: Which economic change would increase the problem of scarcity?

options.text: a decrease in fish stocks
a discovery of a new oil field
an increase in labour productivity
a reduction in waste

questions.questionText: What is a function of a commercial bank?

options.text: acting as the lender of last resort
deciding what is a legal tender
determining monetary policy
providing overdrafts

questions.questionText:
The diagram shows the demand for and the supply of bread.
price
quantity

options.text: a movement of the demand curve to the right
a movement of the supply curve to the right
a shortage of bread
a surplus of bread

questions.questionText: What is an example of occupational mobility of labour?

options.text: A Japanese car manufacturer locates in England.
A nurse returns to work after her children have grown up.
A student takes an evening job in a restaurant.
Farm workers retrain as call-centre workers.

questions.questionText: A person is most likely to save more when there is an increase in a country’s

options.text: exchange rate.
inflation rate.
interest rates.
money supply.

questions.questionText:
One of the functions of money is to act as a measure of value.
What does this mean?

options.text: Money allows people to borrow and lend.
Money allows people to save their surplus income.
Money is used to buy goods and services.
Money is used to compare the worth of different goods and services.

questions.questionText: What is a function of a trade union?

options.text: to negotiate workers’ contracts
to promote workers to more responsible jobs
to recruit workers for the firm
to supervise the workers in the firm

questions.questionText:
A firm which sells its product for $6 has the following total costs.
output (units) 0 10 20 30
total costs ($) 40 100 120 150
Which statement is correct?

options.text: Average cost is lowest when 10 units are produced.
The firm breaks even when 20 units are sold.
The firm has no fixed costs.
Total variable costs fall continuously over these outputs.

questions.questionText:
In August 2008, Infosys, an Indian information technology company, bought Axon, a UK
information technology company.
Which type of integration is this?

options.text: conglomerate
horizontal
vertical backwards
vertical forwards

questions.questionText:
South African companies are planning to undertake major investment in Zimbabwe in order to
mine platinum.
If this investment occurs, what would happen in the short term to the supply of platinum, the price
of platinum and the profits of the companies?
supply curve price of platinum profits of the companies

options.text: no change rise rise
shift to left no change fall
shift to right rise rise
shift to right fall uncertain

questions.questionText: What is correct about a monopoly?

options.text: It may benefit from economies of scale.
It must be privately not state owned.
Its costs are always higher than those of a firm in perfect competition.
It sells only one product.

questions.questionText:
The directors of a firm have to discuss the following topics.
Which topic is least likely to be directly affected by the government’s influence on the firm?

options.text: health and safety laws
the interest it pays on borrowed money
the minimum wage it must pay its workers
the replacement of the director of finance

questions.questionText: What is a direct tax?

options.text: a tax on electricity
a tax on imported goods
a tax on services
a tax on income and wealth

questions.questionText:
A government achieves a high rate of economic growth.
How may this conflict with other government aims?

options.text: It may increase government income.
It may increase incomes for the lower paid.
It may increase the supply of exports.
It may increase the volume of imports.

questions.questionText: What name is given to the type of unemployment that occurs while people search for new jobs?

options.text: cyclical
frictional
residual
structural

questions.questionText:
Between 2002 and 2007, approximately 18 million Latin American households moved out of
poverty.
Which change in the region is most likely to have caused this fall in poverty?

options.text: an increase in economic growth
an increase in inflation
a reduction in employment
a reduction in exports

questions.questionText:
India has a more evenly distributed income than China but a greater proportion of its population
living on less than $1 a day.
What can be concluded from this statement?

options.text: China has a smaller proportion of very rich people.
India has a greater proportion of poor people.
Most of the population of India live on $1 a day.
The average income in China is higher than that in India.

questions.questionText:
Why is the Human Development Index (HDI) a better indicator of comparative living standards
than Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per head?

options.text: It includes international trade.
It includes more measures of living standards.
It is measured in money terms.
It is more directly linked to economic growth.

questions.questionText:
Gross Domestic Product (GDP) per capita is commonly used as an indicator of the comparative
level of development in different countries.
What does not lead to difficulties when using this as a comparison between countries?

options.text: different climatic conditions
different international exchange rates
different population growth rates
different rates of inflation

questions.questionText:
Which policy would best enable a government to encourage greater specialisation in the use of
its country’s resources?

options.text: encouraging diversification in industry
protecting small businesses
reducing tariffs on imports into its country
subsidising job creation in rural areas

questions.questionText: What is likely to happen in a developing country as it becomes more developed?

options.text: A lower percentage of people will go to university.
Average life expectancy will rise.
The rate of population growth will increase.
The tertiary sector will decline in importance.

questions.questionText:
There was an increase in the value of the United States (US) dollar against the South African
Rand.
What is a result of this?

options.text: an increase in the number of exports from the US to South Africa
an increase in the number of imports to the US from South Africa
fewer people from the US spend holidays in South Africa
